conviction_note: No single document decides this print. The evidence is two-sided: a guide that needs a heavy Q4 and a DOE-funded HALEU contract that ended on 30 Sep, against a 30%-of-float short at a 52-week low, an undisclosed-value backlog update and Westerman consolidating into Q4. So p_up is 52 on an abs move of 15 (option-implied 12.3, own median 14.7, raised for the crowded short), which gives +0.6. The findings sum to +1.3 because the positioning and backlog items are sized on their own; the two numbers agree in sign and differ in scale, as the core allows.
bar: DISPUTED, so every finding is capped small. Q3 2026 consensus revenue is $55.2m with EPS $0.35 per Earnings Whispers via finviz (https://finviz.com/news/409530/centrus-faces-a-light-quarter-and-a-halved-stock-as-build-out-story-meets-its-test, 2026-10-27). Other aggregators show $72.4m and -$0.21 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/LEU), or $67.2m / $0.04 and $80.3m / $0.42 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LEU/earnings-forecasts). HC Wainwright has -$0.75. The firm bar is the company's FY2026 guide: revenue $450-500m and capital deployment $350-500m, reaffirmed 2026-08-05 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000162828026053433/ex991-10q2026_08x05.htm). Street FY is about $470.6m. H1 revenue was $252.8m (Q1 $76.7m + Q2 $176.1m), so H2 must deliver $197-247m. LEU SWU orders average about $11.7m each, so quarterly revenue is lumpy and Q3 revenue against a $55-80m bar cannot be called.
positioning_check: Short interest 5,933,422 shares, 29.95% of float, 6.8 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15, published 2026-10-26, flat on the prior report (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LEU/short-interest/). A GuruFocus piece of 2026-07-02 had it at 22.28%, so the short has built through the fall. Skew is +1.32 vol points (25d put minus call), which is balanced; put/call OI 1.1. Tape: spot $91.375, -18.4% over 5 days, -37.9% over 20 days, at the 52-week low, -73% from the high, and -54% from the $199.64 offering price of 2026-09-09. Crowded short into a washed-out tape: negatives are shrunk for squeeze risk.

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $450-500m, reaffirmed in August, requires $197-247m in H2 after H1's $252.8m. With Q3 consensus at $55-80m, Q4 has to carry about $120-190m. Revenue depends on lumpy SWU orders (about $11.7m each), and 'well over one-half' of the LEU Centrus delivers is sourced from TENEX under per-shipment Russian export licences. Any trim to the low end, or a Q4 slip into 2027, lands on the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints with no guidance raise sold off: Q3 2025 -14.72% and Q4 2025 (FY guide set) -20.69%. Q1 2026 raised the guide to $450-500m and rose +12.27%. Q2 2026 only reaffirmed it and fell -5.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: The preview names the Q4 load as the issue, so it is partly priced; the -38% 20-day tape may already discount a trim. If a guide cut were fully priced, skew would show a put premium; it shows +1.3, balanced. The size is small because the bar is disputed and the company reaffirmed in August.
findings.independence: Same as the finviz/Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/409530/centrus-faces-a-light-quarter-and-a-halved-stock-as-build-out-story-meets-its-test), which frames Q4 delivery against the FY guide as the test. The TENEX dependency comes from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000162828026053863/leu-20260630.htm). These two documents together are counted once.

findings.finding: The DOE-funded HALEU Operation Contract ran to 30 Sep 2026. DOE said it does not intend to exercise further options and the FY2027 budget has no cascade funding. Yet Q2 Technical Solutions backlog still carried about $0.8B tied to that contract, of a $4.5B total. The Q3 release is the first report after the funding ended: it either removes or impairs that backlog, or announces a private commercial-operation agreement (being negotiated as of the Q2 10-Q). Technical Solutions revenue already fell 21% in Q2, to $22.7m with a $1.7m loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on backlog removal. Technical Solutions weakness was part of the Q2 2026 print, which fell -5.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: The risk was disclosed in August, but the $0.8B is still inside the $4.5B headline backlog every preview quotes, including the finviz preview of 2026-10-27. A headline that shows backlog flat or down despite three new contracts would surprise readers anchored on $4.5B rising. If it were priced, previews would quote backlog ex-HALEU-ops, and they do not.
findings.independence: The Q2 earnings release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000162828026053433/ex991-10q2026_08x05.htm) states the same $0.8B and no-further-options language, so it is the same fact. ANS (https://www.ans.org/news/article-8180/doe-contract-boosts-centruss-haleu-goals-as-urenco-continues-leu-expansion/) confirms the plan to run the cascade commercially. Net of the rest: LEU is about 87% of revenue.

findings.finding: Three supply contracts were signed after the last print, all with undisclosed values and prepayments: X-energy LEU+HALEU (8-K 2026-08-06), Radiant Kaleidos HALEU (2026-09-09) and Antares multi-year HALEU (8-K 2026-09-17). The Q3 release is the first place their backlog value and any prepayment cash can be quantified.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog rose to $4.5B from $3.8B by Q2 2026, and that print fell -5.12%, so backlog growth alone has not been paid. Contract announcements in Sept did not stop the slide from $199 to $91.
findings.why_not_priced: None of the three contracts has a disclosed value (Insider Monkey and securities.io both say so), so no estimate carries a number for them. If the market had a figure, previews would quote a pro-forma backlog above $4.5B; the preview still quotes $4.5B. The item is contingent, offsets the HALEU-ops backlog risk above, and has a weak reaction history, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: Centrus news-release list (https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/category/news-releases/) and World Nuclear News (https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/antares-centrus-sign-multi-year-haleu-contract). Both are the same announcements, not separate evidence.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-16 Centrus closed the Westerman Holdings acquisition for about $116m ($95m cash plus 165,342 shares). The target had about $160m of 2025 revenue, including non-nuclear oil and gas and industrial customers. It is guided 'accretive to adjusted EPS in the first year' and consolidates from mid-Q4, so the FY revenue guide could rise mechanically by the third-party share of roughly 2.5 months of sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide raise at Q1 2026 (to $450-500m) went with +12.27%. No acquisition precedent.
findings.why_not_priced: The $160m revenue figure is only in the Sept 9 prospectus supplement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000110465926106829/tm2625019d3_424b5.htm), not in the deal release. The street FY of $470.6m in the 10-27 preview sits inside the old range with no visible Westerman add. If priced, FY consensus would sit above $480m. This is inference: part of Westerman's revenue is sales to Centrus, which eliminate, and the third-party share is unquantified.
findings.independence: S-3ASR of 2026-11-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065059/000110465926121326/tm2628683d1_s3asr.htm) confirms the closing date and consideration. The prospectus is the only source for the revenue figure.

findings.finding: Margin read-across: in Q2 2026, Centrus LEU cost of sales rose 36% year on year and SWU unit cost 13%, while gross profit fell 7% on 14% revenue growth. On 2026-10-30, Cameco reported a Q3 adjusted loss on inflationary input costs and higher unit costs, with the LT uranium price at $96.50/lb, and fell 9%. Centrus buys uranium and SWU from TENEX and others at market-linked prices, so gross margin pressure likely persisted into Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 showed exactly this compression (gross profit -7%, net income -42%) and fell -5.12%. UBS cut its target to $170 from $195 citing higher operating costs (barchart, undated).
findings.why_not_priced: Cameco's print landed after Centrus last spoke, and estimates are scattered ($0.35 to -$0.75 EPS), which suggests margins are not pinned down. This is a proxy (macro-to-company transmission), and Centrus's own Q2 number already told the market about cost inflation, so it is sized small and shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Centrus's own Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000162828026053433/ex991-10q2026_08x05.htm) and the finviz preview's cost figures. Cameco Q3 coverage: https://www.cp24.com/news/money/2026/10/30/uranium-miner-cameco-reports-43m-q3-profit-revenue-edges-up-from-year-ago/

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print with 29.95% of float short (5.93m shares, 6.8 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15), up from 22.28% in July. It is at its 52-week low, -54% from the $199.64 September offering price and -38% in 20 days. That setup squeezes on any non-negative read: a reaffirmed guide, a backlog increase or a HALEU-ops agreement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large upside prints happen on this name: +33.13% (Feb 2025), +22.01% (May 2025), +12.27% (May 2026). Downside prints since late 2025 were -14.72% and -20.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: The option market prices a symmetric move (skew +1.3, balanced) and no squeeze premium on calls. The October fall was largely sector- and rate-driven (10y at 5.26% on 10-14; Oklo and NuScale -15% in a week, per TIKR 2026-10-20), not company news, so shorts are positioned on beta into a company-specific event. Sized moderately: the drawdown itself is not evidence, only the 30% short-interest number is.
findings.independence: GuruFocus 2026-07-02 had short interest at 22.28% (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8943554/centrus-energy-leu-leads-short-interest-among-energy-stocks). The sector-driven decline is from TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/oklo-and-nuscale-sink-15-in-a-week-is-the-nuclear-selling-overdone).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-29 Centrus said the first new Oak Ridge centrifuge was completed and the full supply chain stood up 'ahead of the previously-announced year-end target', with centrifuges shipping to Ohio and first new capacity in 2029 'as previously announced'. One 2026 operating target is met before the print, giving the build-out a credibility data point for the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell from $103.29 (10-30 close per S-3ASR) to $91.4 after the announcement, so the milestone was not paid on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and was sold into, so it is near zero. It matters only as the evidence management can cite on the call that capex is buying output.
findings.independence: Centrus news list (https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/category/news-releases/), the same announcement.

findings.finding: Financing answered: the 9 Sep raise netted about $489m, on top of $1.87B cash at 30 Jun and $54m of H1 ATM proceeds. It funds a corroborated build-out: first centrifuge done, Westerman bought for vertical integration, Piketon hiring of 175+. The $2B of common warrants are struck at $227-363 against $91 spot, so they carry no near-term dilution. The only new registration, the 2026-11-02 S-3ASR, covers resale of just 165,342 Westerman ESOT shares, about 0.2 days of volume, and is not a primary shelf or ATM.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025 convertible offering coincided with an ~18% fall (itiger). The September 2026 equity raise was followed by a halving of the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: An S-3ASR two days before a print reads as an offering signal to anyone who sees the form type without opening it. The document shows it is a small resale only, which removes a feared negative. It is small because the balance sheet was already known.
findings.independence: The Davis Polk deal summary (https://www.davispolk.com/experience/centrus-500m-stock-and-pre-funded-warrants-and-2b-common-warrants-offering) and the 424B5 use of proceeds (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000110465926106829/tm2625019d3_424b5.htm).

outside_window.finding: The Piketon (American Centrifuge Plant) lease currently expires 2027-10-01. DOE has said it will work toward an extension before 2026-12-31 but has no obligation to. This is stated in the 2026-11-02 S-3ASR risk factors; the 424B5 names the extension as a risk. The call may touch on it, but the decision lands after the window.

Centrus's first Investor Day is in December 2026. Multi-year targets and any pull-forward of 2029 production are more likely there than in the Q3 release, which may hold back forward commentary on the call.

searched_and_found_nothing: DOE waiver decision on uncommitted 2026-2027 TENEX volumes: no 2026 ruling found. The committed 2026-27 waiver (TheFly via TipRanks) is undated in the snippet.
Russian per-shipment export licences or any interruption of TENEX deliveries in Q3/Q4 2026: nothing found.
Analyst rating or target changes in late October / early November 2026: none found beyond the undated UBS cut to $170. AAII says no downgrades in the month to 11-03.
UxC/TradeTech SWU spot or term price for Q3/October 2026: paywalled, not found.
Specific cause of the 10-30 to 11-04 slide ($103.29 to $91.4): no company news found. Sector and rate moves are the only explanation in the record, and the absence of a cause is not filed.
Whether a private commercial-operation agreement for the HALEU cascade was signed after 30 Sep 2026: no announcement found on the company news list.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (+1.3), so the slight positive lean does not fight the option market; it does cut against a -38% 20-day run-up and two consecutive post-print sell-offs, which is why p_up sits at 52 and not higher despite the 30% short interest.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, 30% of float): the guidance-load negative went from -1.0 to -0.8, the HALEU-ops backlog negative from -1.0 to -0.8 and the cost-inflation proxy from -0.7 to -0.5.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the positioning finding went from +1.5 to +1.2, so it rests only on the sourced short-interest number and not on the size of the fall.
Rule 6 (disputed bar): all findings were already capped at 1.5 or less; print_vs_bar left at 0 because consensus runs from $55m to $80m.
Rules 4 and 2 left standing: financing was already signed after asking what the money buys (a corroborated build-out), and the Westerman item was already filed as guidance.
